content.text:
Since this happened with another GitHub account, **check whether Torque’s GitHub App is private**. Private apps can only be installed on the owning account. [GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/making-a-github-app-public-or-private).

Using the account that created the app:

1. Open **GitHub Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → Torque**.
2. Check **Advanced → Make public** if other accounts should use it.
3. Retry connecting from Torque with the other account.

This is a possible cause, not confirmed yet. **Paste the 404 page’s URL, excluding everything after `?`**, so I can identify whether the failing link is authorization or installation.

content.text:
The URL confirms **GitHub is rejecting the authorization request before returning to Torque**.

If your original account still works, the app’s visibility is the first setting to check:

1. Sign into the account that created Torque’s GitHub App.
2. Open [GitHub App settings](https://github.com/settings/apps) → select Torque → **Advanced**.
3. If it’s private, choose **Make public** so other accounts can authorize it. [GitHub’s visibility rules](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/making-a-github-app-public-or-private).
4. Return to Torque and click **Connect GitHub** again to start a fresh login.

If it’s already public, compare its **Client ID** with `Iv23liYX91FHH3hctmnz`, which Torque is currently sending.

**Does login still work with your original GitHub account?**

## My request:
but why is it showing my name, i mean TORQUE by davies .......

GitHub shows **“Torque by Davies…”** because your personal GitHub account owns the app. Making it public lets other people use it; it doesn’t change its owner.

That name identifies the app’s creator, **not the person logging in**.

If you want it to say **“Torque by [your organization]”**, you’d need to transfer the GitHub App to a GitHub organization.

content.text:
First, create a GitHub organization for your brand if you don’t already have one: [Create an organization](https://github.com/organizations/plan).

Then, signed into the account that owns the Torque app:

1. Open [GitHub App settings](https://github.com/settings/apps).
2. Select **Torque**.
3. Click **Advanced → Transfer ownership**.
4. Enter your organization’s GitHub username and select it from the dropdown.
5. Review any warning, then click **Transfer this GitHub App**. [Official instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/maintaining-github-apps/transferring-ownership-of-a-github-app).

Afterward, start a fresh Torque login to check the owner label. Keep the app **public** so other accounts can continue using it.
